summary.pack_description:
Opening Ice: Elites returns for Series 2 to capture more unforgettable moments when the game's current stars scored their first NHL career goal, or a talented goalie secured his debut NHL victory. Experience the sheer joy and determination as they find the back of the net, or defend their crease in their milestone highlights. Featuring first career milestones from Brady Tkachuk, Brad Marchand, Artemi Panarin, William Nylander, Mikko Rantanen, Jake Oettinger, and more! 

Each pack contains 1 Opening Ice: Elites highlight, 1 Light the Lamp: Legacy highlight, 2 mystery Core highlights that could be from Base 2024-25 (50%), or Across the Pond (50%), and 1 mystery highlight that could be from Base 2024-25 (25%), Light the Lamp: Legacy (20%), Fresh Sweaters (15%), Across the Pond (15%), Opening Ice: Elites (13%), Cause for a Celly: 2010s (7%), or Opening Ice: Icons (5%).

release.name: Opening Ice: Elites Debut LE (Rare)
release.description:
Sale Starts: Monday, Nov 25 at 1pm ET / 10am PT

Sweepstakes: Each pack purchased between Jan 3, 2025 at 12:01:01am ET and Jan 18, 2025 at 11:59:59pm ET is an entry for a chance to win a trip to the NHL Stadium Series™ . Read the blog announcement and official rules (version Française) for more information. No purchase necessary to enter.

 

Price: $65 USD

# Packs Available: 1500 packs total. Edition numbers are distributed randomly.

 

Purchase Limit: Thirty (30) pack limit per person. Once the “Buy Now” process has started, users will have 10 minutes to complete checkout before the pack(s) is released for another collector to purchase.

 

Highlights Per Pack: 5

Pack Contents (Highlight Rarity, Edition Size):

  • One (1) highlight from Opening Ice: Elites (Rare #/250)
  • One (1) highlight from Light the Lamp: Legacy (Limited #/500)
  • Two (2) highlights with the following probabilities:
    • 50% Base 2024-25 (Core #/1500)
    • 50% Across the Pond (Core #/1500)
  • One (1) highlight with the following probabilities:
    • 25% Base 2024-25 (Core #/1500)
    • 20% Light the Lamp: Legacy (Limited #/500) 
    • 15% Fresh Sweaters (Core #/1500)
    • 15% Across the Pond (Core #/1500)
    • 13% Opening Ice: Elites (Rare #/250) 
    • 7% Cause for a Celly: 2010s (Epic #/100)
    • 5% Opening Ice: Icons (Rare #/250) 

 

Payment Methods Accepted: Most major credit and debit cards. Payments will be made via registered payment processor MoonPay where available; where not available, payments will be processed via Stripe. Payment via cryptocurrency is also available. See these FAQs for a complete list of supported currencies.

 

Fan Marketplace: Packs and highlights are eligible to be sold to other collectors in the NHL Breakaway fan marketplace. See FAQ.

 

Transferability: Packs and highlights can be exchanged in the Trade Lounge™ with other NHL Breakaway users.

 

Blockchain: Polygon

 

Sets Included: Highlights List

Collection Guarantee: Series 2 highlights will only be distributed during Series 2, which ends prior to the start of the 2025-26 Regular Season. We will not issue more than the edition limit we have set. Any editions not distributed in packs will not be distributed after the series end date (See FAQ for “Uncirculated Editions”)

 

All sales subject to Terms

summary.name: Cole Caufield
summary.description:
Some career first goals stand out more than others, and Cole Caufield’s was certainly memorable. He scored his first goal as an overtime game winner in front of the home crowd in Montreal. During a 3-on-3 overtime against the Ottawa Senators, Caufield slipped behind the defenders and skated hard toward the net. Jeff Petry spotted him unguarded and fed him the puck, allowing Caufield to redirect it in for his inaugural tally.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Devon Toews
summary.description:
In an overtime matchup against the Chicago Blackhawks, defenseman Devon Toews scored his first NHL goal. After the puck was cycled around, Toews received a pass and unleashed a one-timer that was stopped, but the rebound kicked back out to him. He capitalized on the opportunity, burying the puck for the game winner. Toews spent his first two seasons with the New York Islanders before eventually joining the Colorado Avalanche.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Jason Robertson
summary.description:
Jason Robertson, selected 39th overall in the 2017 NHL Draft, averaged nearly a point per game in his first full NHL season, recording 45 points in 51 games. In early February 2021, he scored his first career goal against Chicago. As the puck was moved to the point, a shot redirected off the goalie’s glove, deflected off Robertson, and went into the net. This game-tying goal in the third period helped the Stars secure a point in the contest.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Nick Suzuki
summary.description:
In the final minute of the first period against the Minnesota Wild, Nick Suzuki netted his first career goal on home ice. After Jeff Petry's one-timer was partially blocked, the puck deflected over to Suzuki, who buried a backhander into the net. Suzuki finished the 2019-20 season with a strong rookie performance, tallying 13 goals and 41 points.

summary.name: Noah Dobson
summary.description:
Chosen 12th overall in the 2018 NHL Draft by the New York Islanders, Noah Dobson is a smooth-skating, puck-moving defenseman. Following an offensive zone faceoff win, the puck was worked over to Dobson, who sent a shot toward the net through heavy traffic. It deflected off the hand of a Detroit player and into the net, marking Dobson's first career goal.

summary.name: Quinn Hughes
summary.description:
Selected 7th overall by the Canucks in the 2018 NHL Draft, Quinn Hughes entered the League with high expectations as a smooth-skating, skilled defenseman—and he delivered. In the Canucks' 2019-20 home opener against the Los Angeles Kings, Hughes scored his first career goal with a power-play slapshot that beat the goaltender. After appearing in just five games the previous season, Hughes finished his first full NHL campaign with an impressive 53 points in 68 games.

summary.name: Seth Jarvis
summary.description:
With his impressive speed, gifted skater Seth Jarvis scored his first career goal in just his second NHL game. After forcing a turnover at the defensive blue line, Jarvis raced down the ice with the puck, outpacing the defender. As he approached the net with a defending player in pursuit, Jarvis lost control of the puck. However, the puck, already in forward motion, continued its path and slipped through the five-hole into the back of the net.

summary.name: Troy Terry
summary.description:
During an Anaheim Ducks power play against the New Jersey Devils, Troy Terry received a pass, skated in, and fired a wrist shot through traffic that found the back of the net for his first career goal. The Colorado-born forward has been a remarkable find for the Ducks, who selected him in the fifth round of the 2015 NHL Draft.

summary.name: Artemi Panarin
summary.description:
In his NHL debut Oct. 7, 2015, against the New York Rangers, Artemi Panarin scored his first career goal. As Patrick Kane controlled the puck deep in the Rangers' zone, Panarin skated into the slot. Kane fed him the puck, and Panarin, all alone in front, fired a wrist shot past the goalie to find the back of the net. With 30 goals, 47 assists, and 77 points in the 2015-16 season, Panarin led all rookies in those categories, earning the Calder Trophy as rookie of the year.

summary.name: Brad Marchand
summary.description:
Drafted by the Boston Bruins in the third round of the 2006 NHL Draft, Brad Marchand scored 21 goals in his first full NHL season in 2010-11, after appearing in 20 games the previous year. On Nov. 3, 2010, Marchand netted his first career goal – a shorthanded effort against the Buffalo Sabres to open the scoring on the road. The Bruins went on to win the Stanley Cup that season, with Marchand contributing 19 points in 25 playoff games.

summary.name: Brady Tkachuk
summary.description:
In his second NHL game and first at home, Brady Tkachuk, the fourth overall pick in the 2018 NHL Draft, netted his first career goal. During an Ottawa Senators power play, the feisty and physical forward charged to the net, where the puck deflected off his skate and slipped behind the goalie for his first of two goals in the game. Tkachuk wrapped up his rookie season with 22 goals and 45 points.

Officially Licensed Product of the NHL, NHLPA, and/or NHLAA. All copyright, logos, and marks are the property of their respective owners and are used, under license, by Sweet. All Rights Reserved. [Terms Apply](https://nhlbreakaway.com/terms).

summary.name: Ilya Sorokin
summary.description:
Playing with a two-goal lead early in the second period, rookie goaltender Ilya Sorokin flashed his glove to make a key stop on Henri Jokiharju. Holding the same lead in the third period, Sorokin came up big again with a crucial glove save on Victor Olofsson in the slot. Sorokin’s 20-save effort secured his first career win and shutout during the 2020-21 season, when he recorded 13 wins and three shutouts along with a .918 save percentage and 2.17 goals-against average over 22 games.

summary.name: Jaccob Slavin
summary.description:
Chosen 120th overall by the Carolina Hurricanes in the 2012 NHL Draft, defenseman Jaccob Slavin netted his first career goal during the 2015-16 season on Dec. 8, 2015, against the Dallas Stars. Skating the puck up the ice, Slavin dished it to Eric Staal on the far side before driving to the net. He then buried a rebound sitting in the crease from a Riley Nash shot, scoring his first NHL goal.

summary.name: Jake Oettinger
summary.description:
The only goaltender selected in the first round of the 2017 NHL Draft, Jake Oettinger earned his first career win against the Detroit Red Wings on Jan. 28, 2021. Late in the second period, Oettinger made a series of key saves during a Red Wings power play to preserve the Stars’ two-goal lead. He later denied an attempt from the slot by Bobby Ryan in the third period. Oettinger finished his first NHL start with 20 saves, contributing to a successful debut.

summary.name: Mathew Barzal

Mathew Barzal, renowned for his great ability to transport the puck up the ice, demonstrated his talent in a game against the rival New York Rangers by scoring his first career goal. Skating the puck through the neutral zone, Barzal navigated around his check along the boards and advanced toward the net. He then fired a sharp angle shot that beat the goaltender. Barzal’s remarkable rookie season with the New York Islanders ended with 85 points and earned him the Calder Trophy as rookie of the year.

summary.name: Mikko Rantanen
summary.description:
A big-bodied forward with a powerful shot, Mikko Rantanen was selected 10th overall in the 2015 NHL Draft by the Colorado Avalanche and scored his first career goal Nov. 11, 2016, at home against the Winnipeg Jets. During an Avalanche power play, Rantanen used his excellent shot release to beat the goaltender short-side high for the game's opening goal.

summary.name: Robert Thomas
summary.description:
Selected as the St. Louis Blues' first pick in the 2017 NHL Draft, Robert Thomas has proven to be a standout for the franchise. During his rookie season in 2018-19, Thomas netted his first career goal against the Nashville Predators. After a Predators turnover at the blue line, Brayden Schenn sent the puck to Thomas, positioned near the faceoff dot on the far side. Thomas collected the puck, took a quick glance, and fired a wrist shot top shelf on the far side, marking his milestone goal.

Early in the third period in a game against the Anaheim Ducks, Roman Josi scored his first NHL goal on a power play. After receiving a pass from fellow defenseman Shea Weber, Josi fired a slapshot from the point through a screen, beating the goaltender. His goal gave Nashville its first lead of the game, which they held on to for the win.

In just his fourth NHL game, William Nylander scored his first career goal at home against the Ottawa Senators. After a Toronto faceoff win in the offensive zone, Nylander collected the puck, skated into the slot, and fired a wrist shot that beat the goalie for his inaugural tally. Nylander recorded 13 points in 22 games during the 2015-16 season, and followed it up with 61 points the next season.

summary.description:
Connor McDavid, known for his sensational and electrifying play, set Edmonton ablaze early in the 2021-22 season. Late in the third period, trailing by a goal, McDavid executed the unthinkable by weaving through four defenders and then deking out the netminder with just under three minutes remaining to score the tying goal. That same season, McDavid would secure his fourth Art Ross Trophy leading the league in points in only his seventh season in the league.

Starting with a backcheck and a strip of the puck, Evgeni Malkin scored a beautiful unassisted goal. In one fluid motion, Malkin executed a spin-o-rama and sniped a backhander bar-down for a sensational goal. Later that 2015-16 season, Malkin won his second Stanley Cup – and first of back-to-back championships that boosted his career total to three (all with the Penguins).

summary.name: Jonathan Toews

As a child, Jonathan Toews idolized Joe Sakic, and in his fifth NHL game of his rookie season, he faced off against his hero, donning the same jersey number 19 that Sakic wore. During that game, Toews scored a spectacular goal that electrified the home crowd. Early in the first period of a scoreless game, he weaved through three Colorado defenders, deked the goalie, and tucked the puck into the net. Toews finished his rookie season with 24 goals and 54 points in 64 games, and later won three Stanley Cups with Chicago.

During the 2016-17 season, the deceptive Nikita Kucherov scored a memorable shootout goal that decided the game against Buffalo. As Kucherov approached the netminder, he faked a shot and let the puck slide past the fooled goalie into the net. Kucherov continues to climb the all-time ranks in franchise history, averaging 1.20 points per game through his first 10 years in the league, all with Tampa Bay.

summary.name: Rick Nash

In the final minute of the third period of a tied game, Rick Nash scored a sensational, unforgettable goal. Disrupting the play at the blueline, Nash headed up the ice and received a pass, setting up a 1-on-2 rush. He skillfully stickhandled through two Coyotes defenders, deked the goalie, and fired the puck into the open net for the game-winner. Nash spent 9 of his 15 NHL seasons with the Blue Jackets and left as the franchise leader in goals, assists and points.

Ryan Getzlaf, the all-time points leader for the Anaheim Ducks, scored a remarkable shorthanded goal during the 2017-18 season. In the defensive zone, while attempting to clear the puck, Getzlaf lofted it high into the air and chased it down. As the puck settled near the high slot, the goalie came out of the net to swat it away. However, Getzlaf reached it first, chipped it past the netminder, and shot it into the net.

summary.name: Sidney Crosby

Sidney Crosby has scored many spectacular goals throughout his storied career, but one particularly memorable moment came during a game against Edmonton in the 2018-19 season. In overtime, Crosby carried the puck into the offensive zone, skated it below the goal line, and maneuvered through two defenders to get in front of the net. He held onto the puck until reaching the far side of the goal, where he fired a backhander into the net. That season, Crosby finished with 100 points, marking the sixth time in his career he reached the century mark in a single season.

Chara spent 14 of his 24-year career in Boston, where he won a Norris Trophy in 2009 and captained the team to a Stanley Cup championship in 2011.

As he skated towards the net in the slot, Lafrenière faked a shot, freezing the defender. With a deft lift of a defender's stick, Giroux broke through the check, maneuvered around the goalie, and calmly deposited the puck into the net.

summary.name: Mathew Barzal
summary.description:
Mathew Barzal, renowned for his great ability to transport the puck up the ice, demonstrated his talent in a game against the rival New York Rangers by scoring his first career goal. Skating the puck through the neutral zone, Barzal navigated around his check along the boards and advanced toward the net. He then fired a sharp angle shot that beat the goaltender. Barzal’s remarkable rookie season with the New York Islanders ended with 85 points and earned him the Calder Trophy as rookie of the year.

summary.name: Mikko Rantanen
summary.description:
A big-bodied forward with a powerful shot, Mikko Rantanen was selected 10th overall in the 2015 NHL Draft by the Colorado Avalanche and scored his first career goal Nov. 11, 2016, at home against the Winnipeg Jets. During an Avalanche power play, Rantanen used his excellent shot release to beat the goaltender short-side high for the game's opening goal.

summary.name: Robert Thomas
summary.description:
Selected as the St. Louis Blues' first pick in the 2017 NHL Draft, Robert Thomas has proven to be a standout for the franchise. During his rookie season in 2018-19, Thomas netted his first career goal against the Nashville Predators. After a Predators turnover at the blue line, Brayden Schenn sent the puck to Thomas, positioned near the faceoff dot on the far side. Thomas collected the puck, took a quick glance, and fired a wrist shot top shelf on the far side, marking his milestone goal.

summary.name: Roman Josi
summary.description:
Early in the third period in a game against the Anaheim Ducks, Roman Josi scored his first NHL goal on a power play. After receiving a pass from fellow defenseman Shea Weber, Josi fired a slapshot from the point through a screen, beating the goaltender. His goal gave Nashville its first lead of the game, which they held on to for the win.

summary.name: William Nylander
summary.description:
In just his fourth NHL game, William Nylander scored his first career goal at home against the Ottawa Senators. After a Toronto faceoff win in the offensive zone, Nylander collected the puck, skated into the slot, and fired a wrist shot that beat the goalie for his inaugural tally. Nylander recorded 13 points in 22 games during the 2015-16 season, and followed it up with 61 points the next season.

Opening Ice: Elites returns for Series 2 to capture more unforgettable moments when the game's current stars scored their first NHL career goal, or a talented goalie secured his debut NHL victory. Experience the sheer joy and determination as they find the back of the net, or defend their crease in their milestone highlights. Featuring first career milestones from Brady Tkachuk, Brad Marchand, Artemi Panarin, William Nylander, Mikko Rantanen, Jake Oettinger, and more! 

Each pack contains 1 Opening Ice: Elites highlight, 1 Light the Lamp: Legacy highlight, 2 mystery Core highlights that could be from Base 2024-25 (50%), or Across the Pond (50%), and 1 mystery highlight that could be from Base 2024-25 (25%), Light the Lamp: Legacy (20%), Fresh Sweaters (15%), Across the Pond (15%), Opening Ice: Elites (13%), Cause for a Celly: 2010s (7%), or Opening Ice: Icons (5%).
